# GTA: Vice City, Archipelago v1.0.0

## What randomization does

Missions no longer unlock each other. Every mission giver's strand opens one mission at a time, and only when the multiworld sends you the progressive unlock for that giver, so the order you play the city in is decided by the seed rather than by the story.

Crossing to the mainland is an item, and so is Starfish Island. The bridges stay shut until the multiworld hands you the way over.

Missions and activities stop paying their vanilla rewards. The check is the reward, and the money that mission would have paid goes back into the item pool as filler.

The one mission that needs no item is the first Rosenberg meeting, which is open on a new game and is where every seed starts.

## Checks

492 with every class enabled. Story missions are always on; every other class is a YAML toggle, and a disabled class behaves fully vanilla, keeping its own rewards and holding no checks.

| Check class | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| Story missions | 44 |
| Hidden packages | 100 |
| Rampages | 35 |
| Unique stunt jumps | 36 |
| Emergency vehicle milestones | 56 |
| Properties and venue missions | 40 |
| Robbable stores | 15 |
| Side events | 14 |
| Ambient pickups | 116 |
| Shop items | 36 |

The emergency milestones are per level. The side events are the stadium events, the chopper checkpoints, the RC missions, Cone Crazy, PCJ Playground, Trial by Dirt and Test Track.

## Goals

- **Final mission.** Complete "Keep Your Friends Close...".
- **Hidden package hunt.** Receive a configurable number of Package Fragments from the multiworld, the macguffin of this world. Collecting a Hidden Package in game stays an ordinary check and is never goal progress. The last fragment finishes your run, and warps to the ending cutscene.
- **The game's own 100 percent.** The completion percentage Vice City itself tracks.

## Options

**Ability locks.** Sprint, jump, crouch, vehicles, weapon equipping and your wallet can each be taken away and put in the pool. Vehicles split into land, sea and air vehicles. With the wallet locked, cash is void until it arrives.

**Content locks.** Hidden packages, rampages, stunt jumps, properties and robbable stores can be held inert until their item arrives. Packages and icons are absent from the world, a locked stunt jump flies but registers nothing, and aiming at a shopkeeper starts no robbery. Split them city-wide, per district, or per district per class, which is 42 items at the finest setting against 5 with the locks whole.

**Shuffles.** The 9 radio stations become items, and you start with one. The minimap can start hidden. The ambient pickups can trade places among themselves. The five emergency vehicle finish rewards, infinite sprint, fireproof, max armor, the taxi jump and max health, can go into the pool.

**Mainland access** can split into one item per bridge instead of a single flip.

**Traps** take a configurable share of the filler, default 15 percent, spread over seven types: raised wanted level, hostile pedestrians, stormy weather, foggy weather, sped up time, slowed time and drunk vision.

**DeathLink** is supported and off by default. It sends on Wasted only, so an arrest is not a death, and the client can toggle it for a session without regenerating.

## In game

Received items slide in down the left edge of the screen, naming the item, who it came from and where it was found. Items apply as they arrive, including in the middle of a mission.

The pause menu carries an **ARCHIPELAGO** page above Quit Game: client connection, checks sent, items received, the game's own completion percentage, which crossings are open, whichever locks, stations and minimap setting the seed configured, and the last messages in full.

Two optional classes put a check on an object. An ambient pickup still holding its check spins as a GTA III logo, the one sprite the game never uses, and a shop stand holding its check sells "AP Item" in place of its stock, with the same GTA III logo.

## Trackers

Universal Tracker is supported and works out of the box.

A PopTracker pack ships alongside this release: <https://github.com/Kryen112/GTAVC_AP_Poptracker>

## Installing

You need **Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer** and the original classic PC release of GTA: Vice City, executable version 1.0, with its original `data/main.scm`. This is the classic game and not the Definitive Edition, which the mod does not run on.

You also need two free community tools in your game folder, [Ultimate ASI Loader](https://github.com/ThirteenAG/Ultimate-ASI-Loader) and [CLEO](https://github.com/cleolibrary/III.VC.CLEO).

Then install `gta_vice_city.apworld`. This holds the world, the client and the in-game mod; there is no separate mod download. Open the **GTA Vice City Client** from the Archipelago Launcher, connect, point it at your game folder once, and it installs the mod and launches the game for you.

Each seed gets its own save slots, so your existing Vice City saves are left untouched.

The setup guide covers all of it, including what to do when something goes wrong: <https://github.com/Kryen112/GTA-Vice-City-AP/blob/main/apworld/gta_vice_city/docs/setup_en.md>
